summary.motor: UB SEDS N2O hybrid, static test fire 2026-11-16 (local evening; GS recording timestamped 2026-11-17 00:59:46 UTC)
summary.burn_time_definition: time thrust >= 5% of peak (144 N), t=0.01 s to 4.6 s on the CSV timebase; thrust reaches 0 at 5.35 s. Liquid phase (tank-pressure knee) ends about 2.7 s; after that comes a vapor-phase tail decaying from about 1.7 kN to 0
summary.peak_thrust_note: startup peak at t~0.7 s (measured 260-340 kgf samples). The 0.2-0.55 s hold at 2734 N is interpolated, not measured; if that segment was higher the peak could be ~3.1 kN
summary.liquid_phase_plateau_n: about 2.0 kN decaying to 1.7 kN (t 0.9-2.7 s)

propellant_mass_breakdown.oxidizer_how: DAQ KG50 fill load cell (LOADCELL_50_WEIGHT_KG) read 5.5-5.65 kg (LOADCELL_FILL_PERCENT 70.4% of 8 kg target) during the ~9 s before the main valve opened. Assumes the fill tare was good. Post-fire KG50 is unusable (it reads -6.2 kg and drifts), so actual ox consumed is not measured; residual vapor may mean slightly less than 5.6 kg was burned
propellant_mass_breakdown.fuel_how: NOT measured; no fuel grain mass found in repos. Assumed O/F 5 (range 3.5-7), i.e. 0.8-1.6 kg

summary.delivered_isp_s: about 107 s (7050 N*s / (6.7 kg * 9.807)); range ~85-135 s. Low compared with an ideal hybrid (180-220 s), which is typical of a small test motor with a long vapor tail. It is also possible that KG50 overstates the ox or KG1000 understates thrust
summary.t0_definition: CSV t=0 is the valve-open time + 0.1 s (VB VALVE_STATE valve[0]=1 received at recording t=9.188 s; mapped to the DAQ clock with the median DAQ receive-source offset of 19 ms). The 0.1 s ignition delay matches the 2026-10-31 fire, where chamber pressure rose 0.16 s after valve open
summary.flight_use_note: About 7 kN*s is probably well short of 10k ft for a 6 in x ~4.6 m rocket (that usually needs ~10-20 kN*s depending on mass). If the mock flight must reach 10k ft, scale the curve's thrust axis (or burn time) and state that it is scaled.

sources.fetched: 2026-11-22 via HTTP GET only (route GET /api/recordings/{id}/csv, GroundStation26 backend/src/recording_export.rs)
sources.fire_window: recording t=9.19 s (valve open, = 2026-11-17 00:59:55 UTC) to t~14.6 s
sources.channels_used: DAQ LOADCELL_WEIGHT_KG (calibrated KG1000 = 1000 kg thrust cell; test-fire mode labels this channel as thrust), VB PRESSURE_TRANSDUCER_CALIBRATED (ox tank PT, PX309-1KG5V), DAQ LOADCELL_50_WEIGHT_KG (KG50 fill cell), VB VALVE_STATE
sources.kg1000_calibration_in_recording: kg = 9481.62 * raw - 116.03 (linear; fitted from raw/calibrated pairs in the recording, residual 0. Same coefficients as the 2026-10-31 recording). The gain was not independently verified

sources.role: CROSS-CHECK: chamber pressure and burn duration from the last fire with a working chamber PT
sources.fire_window: valve open at recording t=10.04 s (2026-10-31 18:57:34 UTC = 14:57 EDT); Pc rises at 10.20 s and falls to baseline at ~16.25 s
sources.findings: Chamber PT (COMBUSTION_CHAMBER_PRESSURE): startup peak 43 psig, then 38 psig decaying to 19 psig over 10.25-15.4 s, collapsing at liquid runout ~15.5 s. Pc above 5% of peak lasts ~6.0 s; liquid phase ~5.3 s. Ox tank 343 -> 226 psi, then crashes at runout. KG50 fill cell: 3.98 kg before, 0.66 kg after, so ~3.3 kg ox consumed (4.0 kg loaded). KG1000 showed NO thrust (raw unchanged at 0.01231 V apart from isolated spikes up to 127 kg), so the load cell was not reading in the thrust path on this fire

steps: Take DAQ LOADCELL_WEIGHT_KG samples (40 Hz) on DAQ source timestamps. Receive-time batching gaps (e.g. 10.14-10.49 s) are not real gaps; the source clock is continuous
Reject rails and open-lead artifacts (values >= 600 or <= -50 kg; the channel rails at 1726 kg and -96 kg)
Subtract the post-burn baseline of -1.33 kg (median, 7-11 s after valve open). The pre-burn baseline is unusable because the channel was railed at 1726 kg
Apply a 5-sample rolling median, 0.05 s bin means, then two 3-point moving averages

The 2.59-2.83 s (valve-relative) cluster at liquid runout (values 2-449 kg alternating) is replaced by linear interpolation; its block mean (~212 kg) was close to its neighbours, so the impulse effect is about 60 N*s

Valve-relative 0-0.65 s has no trustworthy data (open-lead rail/garbage mix). Filled with an assumed ramp 0 -> 2734 N over 0.1-0.3 s and a hold to the first good sample. The ox tank pressure starts dropping immediately at valve open, and the 10-31 fire lit within 0.16 s, so prompt ignition is the nominal assumption
Trapezoid-integrate; burn ends when thrust drops below 0.5 kgf
method_1_loadcell_integration.uncertainty_budget: startup gap -1.1/+0.5 kN*s; KG1000 gain unverified and an open lead / DAQ supply intermittent were present, so add +/-10% for calibration; combined range 5.4-8.3 kN*s

method_2_chamber_pressure_x_Cf_x_At.reason: No throat or exit diameter, nozzle drawing, or motor design file exists in any repo (searched GroundStation26, DAQ-Board, FlightComputer26, FirmwareSimulator, reports, research_notes for throat/nozzle/Isp/impulse). The measured 2026-10-31 Pc (35-43 psig, i.e. ~50-58 psia, only ~10% of tank pressure) is also implausibly low for a ~2 kN hybrid: at Pc ~50 psia, 1.8 kN would need a throat of ~75 mm. Either that fire was a weak or different configuration, or the PT reading was off. The firmware divider/200 psi/V scaling at commits ee45a1b/2cf3b9b looks correct, so the cause was not found. Pc was used only for burn timing and shape. The 2026-11-16 fire had the chamber PT intentionally disconnected (0 psi / ~0.009-0.02 V flat)

method_3_ox_mass_x_assumed_isp.status: COMPUTED as a bound only; disagrees with method 1
method_3_ox_mass_x_assumed_isp.fire_2026_11_16: m_prop ~6.7 kg (5.6 ox + ~1.1 fuel assumed) x Isp 180-220 s gives 11.8-14.5 kN*s, 1.7-2x the measured load-cell impulse. Ideal Isp is not reached by this test motor (or KG50 ox is overstated / KG1000 thrust understated). Treat it as an upper bound only
method_3_ox_mass_x_assumed_isp.fire_2026_10_31: ~3.3 kg ox consumed (+0.5-0.9 kg fuel) gives 6.9-8.6 kN*s at 180-220 s, or ~4.3-5.2 kN*s at the ~107 s delivered Isp seen on 11-16

methods.method_4_cross_check: Burn-shape consistency: both fires show a liquid phase (11-16: ~2.7 s at ~404 psi start; 10-31: ~5.3 s at ~343 psi start) followed by a vapor tail, and on 11-16 the thrust tail tracks the tank-pressure blowdown. Flow rates differ a lot (11-16 ~2 kg/s ox in the liquid phase vs 10-31 ~0.7 kg/s), so the two fires probably used different injector or plumbing configurations. The 10-31 timing should not be merged into the 11-16 curve

unusable_or_rejected_data: 2026-11-16 fire KG1000: railed at 1726 kg (raw 0.194 V saturation) before valve open and intermittently for the first ~0.65 s after (open lead), then mostly clean. Isolated glitches at ~2.6-2.8 s

2026-11-16 fire KG50: steps -44 kg exactly while the burn runs and stays flat while thrust decays, so it is not thrust and not ox mass during the burn (electrical/ground offset, consistent with the DAQ supply/ground intermittent). Post-fire value drifts from -6.2 to -3.9 kg over 25 min, so the post-fire ox residual is not measurable
2026-10-31 fire KG1000: no thrust response at all (only isolated spikes), so it cannot give a thrust curve
2026-10-31 fire KG50: also steps about -21 kg during the burn (same artifact); only the pre/post values are used
groundstation_recording_2026-10-30_23-23-48_776.db: valve dump at t=771.8 s; tank 437 psi blew down in ~2 s with no liquid phase, Pc only 17 psig spike, KG1000 flat. A cold-flow/vent, not a fire

groundstation_recording_2026-10-31_15-55-56_744.db and 2026-10-31_18-46-28_413.db: chamber PT flat 0.017 V, no fire. 18-46 ended in an automatic-zero-failure abort; the fire followed in the 18-57 recording
